correctness.rationale: Loday canonical infix tree coordinates give a local Tamari rotation difference exactly (+ac,-ac), hence known length sqrt(2)ac. A marked rotation decomposes uniquely into subtrees A,B,C and a binary context with generating series T/(1-2T), giving M_N(a,c)=C_(a-1)C_(c-1) binom(2(N-a-c),N-a-c)/2. Derivatives yield W_N and growing edge-count mean; fixed a,c asymptotics give independent Catalan marginal probabilities summing to one. Uniform Stirling estimates ac M_N/W_N -> [2πN² sqrt(uv(1-u-v))]^{-1}, with global O(sqrt ε) boundary strips, prove length-biased Dirichlet(1/2,1/2,1/2). Independent complete rotation enumeration for N=3..8 found 1,7,38,187,874,3958 normalized length sums and matched every edge multiplicity. Finite trees are not a proof of the limiting law.
